scope_gaps.note: Both snapshots are about specific things: the Google Account (phone number used for sign-in and recovery) and generic account recovery and 2-step verification (UK NCSC). Neither says anything about giving up a phone number or about Polish providers; the title generalises to all linked accounts.

The NCSC page is UK guidance on recovering a hacked account and on 2-step verification (codes often by SMS or email on email and banking accounts). It does not discuss changing or giving up a phone number, does not say that email or bank providers store the user's phone number, and does not cover Polish banks. The Google page covers Google services only.
The one-week delay for using a new number for sensitive verification is stated only for the Google Account; no snapshot gives it for other providers.
The statement is about Google and Google services only; a reader might assume other providers behave the same, which the sentence does not claim.

The second cited source (NCSC, a UK government agency guidance page) is not vendor documentation and is not named in this description; the description therefore under-describes the cited evidence base. It does not claim more than the sources say.
